Extra pages for standard storage boxes and extra tabs for big storage boxes. L and R switch pages. Each standard page uses one of 271 standard box spots (20 slots each). Each big box tab uses one of 256 big box spots (60 slots each). About the first 22 standard boxes and 42 big boxes placed get every extra. Later boxes get fewer or none. Off during Link Play. Items stay saved. Next start.
With box_tabs: pages per standard storage box, including its first page (a page past this that holds items still shows). Next start.

Tabs per big storage box, including the box itself. At 1, only the box's 3 pages (60 slots) are enabled. At 6, up to 18 pages (360 slots) are enabled. L and R move between tabs at page boundaries. Each tab uses one of the island's 256 big box spots (60 slots each), so about the first 42 big boxes placed get every tab and later boxes get fewer or none. A tab with items stays available if you lower this. Extra tabs are off during Link Play. Items stay saved. Next start.

Launcher only (online.rs): while the game runs, tell the Recompia online server that this player is online, with the launcher's online name, version, Windows or Linux and the creatures-at-home count. Sends data off the PC, so off by default.
The game is told it has an internet connection, so events that need one the first time (Apples to Applin) can start. Nothing is sent: online services still fail. Next start.
On a phone, the 3D picture's resolution in percent of the screen per side, 15 to 100 (0: worked out once from [display] render_scale and [upscale] scene_scale, the keys before it).

On a phone with Dynamic Resolution: gpu follows the GPU's time per frame; thermal also caps the resolution by the phone's thermal headroom (dynamic_resolution_headroom, same section), so the GPU can run at lower clocks before the phone throttles.
With dynamic_resolution_mode = thermal: the thermal headroom to hold (1.0 = the severe throttling status; about 0.033 per degree C); the device's light-throttling threshold minus 0.03 when lower.

Written by a phone's Dynamic Resolution: what it learned (the settled percent, its floor, the thermal cap) for one screen, mode, Resolution, upscaler and frame cap, so the next start begins there. Cleared by deleting it.
